Renée Slegers said losing four points was not what they wanted, but that they were still only in the third week of the season. According to the Guardian, Arsenal were four points behind Manchester City after three matches.

items.descriptionTR:
Read what England's new Test coach Stephen Fleming had to say about Bazball, Ben Stokes, the team's discipline issues and his own philosophy.
￼
Fleming has joined England on a four-year deal [Getty Images]
Stephen Fleming has given his first interviews since becoming England's Test coach.
The New Zealander, who replaces his close friend Brendon McCullum, spoke at length - covering Bazball, Ben Stokes' departure, England's discipline problems, his own coaching style and more.
Here's what he had to say...
Fleming on Carse and England's discipline problems
England have been dogged by off-field issues in recent times. Harry Brook was involved in an altercation with a nightclub bouncer last year, Ben Duckett was videoed apparently drunk in Australia, Stokes and Gus Atkinson broke a team curfew and Brydon Carse was investigated by police after an incident in Derby.
Fleming said: "It's been disappointing, because I understand what people are working towards. These events can derail a lot of things and divert attention from what really matters.
"When I look at epitomising an international cricketer and what they should stand for, it's Joe [Root].
"When he sits in an interview and openly expresses his disappointment, or uses "hacked off", I know there's work to be done.
"Also, the belonging, identity, what are we doing here together and how we can be the best version of ourselves. A lot of that work has begun.
"That's one of the key things for me to develop and my work with Joe has begun."
On Carse, specifically, Fleming said the bowler is available for selection but added: "There are standards. We pick on runs and wickets primarily, but I think it's foolish not to also say there are standards that need to be set."
On his relationship with McCullum
￼
Fleming joked he is like McCullum's big brother [Getty Images]
Fleming has a long-standing relationship with McCullum as a former team-mate, friend and business partner. He replaces his fellow Black Cap, whose tenure as Test coach began with stunning highs before turning sour with the Ashes defeat and his sacking this summer.
"He was heart-sore it had worked out that way, but he was incredibly positive about the experience and opportunity.
"He's been unwavering on that. His belief about where these teams can go is strong, and that was a major part when I was talking to him about doing the role.
"I love his confidence and aggressive nature. I'm more measured.
"Somewhere in between we've got a beautiful working relationship with a huge amount of respect.
"I have so much respect for what Ben Stokes and Brendon did for this English side. They changed the landscape of cricket and that's a really powerful thing."
On what went wrong with Bazball
McCullum's side beat New Zealand and South Africa in their first summer before a memorable win in Pakistan. They were unable to win any of their five-Test series against India and Australia, however.
"I was in awe of what that team were doing and how they were doing it.
"The last 12 months, the evolution – teams caught up, there was talent lost, a lot of reasons. That's now my opportunity.
"There was a thousand wickets lost – [James] Anderson, [Stuart] Broad, then [Chris] Woakes.
"When you do something special and you start doing it differently, everybody else takes a bit of time, then they catch up.
"The pressure then goes on to evolution and that can create some challenges. That's my take on it.
"The Ashes wasn't what they wanted and that is what this team is measured on.
"All I can think about is now my opportunity to pick it up, and maybe add my style, which is looking at personality, a little bit more measured."
On Stokes
￼
Stokes and McCullum were united as captain and coach in 2022. Their tenure ended after this summer's defeat by New Zealand [Getty Images]
Stokes, who announced his shock retirement in June, played under Fleming at Chennai Super Kings in the Indian Premier League. Fleming revealed the pair spoke at Durham earlier this week.
Fleming said: "He'd just come off another monster bowling spell.
"He was in a great space, really happy, enjoying his time with Durham.
"He's got a good winter planned with the family and is very much at peace with his decision. When a player makes that decision to retire, I respect that decision 100%.
"To try to turn that around and question that is wrong. I know how much goes into that type of decision, and I respect that."
Fleming on his wait to arrive
Fleming was named England coach on 30 July but did not take charge of the recent series win over Pakistan, instead following from home.
Fleming said: "There were commitments and family commitments I had that I just wasn't in a position to break. That's more about me as a person, than dropping everything and coming over here.
"I watched and connected with Joe and the team straight away once it was approved – I've got a stress fracture in my left ear from phone calls.
"Watching remotely, I won't say it was an advantage, but watching them operate with eyes wide open as to what was expected, the opportunity, the challenges, and there was also another part – introducing Joe back into captaincy, and Marcus Trescothick the opportunity to do the head coach's role.
"That's part of why I love the game, bringing people forward, developing people, leadership, and they did brilliantly.
"It gave me an opportunity to catch my breath, and then start pretty fresh with a clear mind about what's ahead."
Fleming on his own coaching style
￼
Fleming led Chennai Super Kings to five Indian Premier League titles before leaving his role as head coach after this year's tournament [Getty Images]
Though Fleming has extensive experience in franchise cricket, he has never coached a red-ball side. He was New Zealand captain for 80 of his 111 Tests, however.
On the playing style he wants, Fleming said: "If people were watching a team, I'd love people to say they are well-planned, there's a discipline and a really strong basic structure to what we're doing, but there's also a bit of flair.
"That's not necessarily me and the way I played, but it's what I loved about this English side when they started playing like this.
"It's taking the best of that and adding that planning aspect, so if supporters could look at us and say 'yeah, they are disciplined, well-planned and competitive'. That's a good start.
"The greatest thing for a team to do is to be able to play conditions and situations.
"One thing this team has earned is the ability to be positive. One of the other aspects is winning the tough moments and making sure we don't just play entertaining cricket and win moments, but win games."
On the Ashes and the World Test Championship
Fleming's first series in charge is against South Africa in December. After two Tests in Bangladesh and a one-off anniversary Test in Melbourne in the winter, attention will then turn to next summer's Ashes. Fleming rejected the idea English cricket is too obsessed by beating Australia.
"No, because I have an obsession with it as well," he said. "New Zealand has an obsession with it, we love it.
"We want to beat Aussie. We're heavily linked to England performances. We have a deep desire to beat Australia in everything, as the little cousin.
"We are linked, and I'm incredibly excited about being part of it. You don't think you're ever going to get that opportunity.
"To have that opportunity and be part of it, I can't wait. I want to be my best self and have a team that represents itself in the best possible way. I've got a vision of that and it's aspirational. It will be brilliant."
On the World Test Championship, an event England are yet to reach the final of, he said: "England could do much better than that.
"And even attitude just around the over rate, I think, comes down to identity and style of play.
"And if that's one of the pinnacle trophies in world cricket, why would we not be trying to get it along with every other marquee event that comes our way?"
	•	'Beat the Aussies' - new England coach Fleming's key aim
￼
items.titleTR: Fleming on England discipline, Stokes, late arrival and coaching styles

items.descriptionTR:
New Zealander hopes to add ‘a bit of cricket sense in the key moments’ to Bazball template
“Flemball? That’s a medical condition.” Stephen Fleming’s first press conference as England Test coach was exactly what you would expect from a man appointed to bring calm to a team that had started to career off course.
While the Manchester rain did its worst outside, Fleming was the handsome sea captain on top of his ship, even if that ship had to float without him during the Test series against Pakistan. England won 3-0 while Fleming saw to family and commercial commitments. But the wait has given him thinking time to work out what he wants to achieve.
items.titleTR: ‘I can’t wait for the Ashes’: new Test coach Fleming wants England to be No 1

slots.packetSpot:
England's new Test coach Stephen Fleming has set out his intention to build a more disciplined, organised team capable of adapting to conditions after Brendon McCullum. While aiming for a competitive setup able to win difficult moments, Fleming wants England to be more ambitious in the World Test Championship and other major tournaments, and to beat Australia in the Ashes.

Fleming, who has taken up the role on a four-year deal, will begin with a series against South Africa in December. Tests in Bangladesh and a one-off Test in Melbourne are then planned, while next summer's Ashes series in England is central to the schedule. England had won only two of the final 10 Tests of the McCullum era, lost the Ashes in Australia 4-1 and had yet to reach a World Test Championship final.

Fleming said runs and wickets would be the priority in selection, but that standards of behaviour also needed to be set. Although Brydon Carse has not been charged by police, he faces a Cricket Regulator investigation; Fleming said the player remained available for selection but that standards existed. He also said he respected Ben Stokes's decision to retire from international cricket and would not try to change it.

items.descriptionTR: Top politicians in Kosovo said the Hague judgment finding ex-President Thaci and three other Kosovo Liberation Army ex-leaders guilty of war crimes was unjust – but a Serbian minister said it proved the KLA was 'criminal'. Top politicians in Kosovo said the Hague judgment finding ex-President Thaci and three other Kosovo Liberation Army ex-leaders guilty of war crimes was unjust – but a Serbian minister said it proved the KLA was 'criminal'.
items.titleTR: Kosovo Slams ‘Unjust’ Conviction of Hashim Thaci; Serbian Minister Applauds

slots.packetSpot:
The Kosovo Specialist Chambers in The Hague convicted former Kosovo Liberation Army members Hashim Thaci, Kadri Veseli, Jakup Krasniqi and Rexhep Selimi of war crimes linked to the 1998-99 conflict. According to the reported sentences, Thaci and Krasniqi were each sentenced to 25 years in prison, Veseli to 18 years and Selimi to 13 years; their lawyers said they would challenge the ruling.

The ruling drew strong reactions in Kosovo. Prime Minister Albin Kurti, Acting President Albulena Haxhiu, the Democratic Party of Kosovo and former Prime Minister Ramush Haradinaj described the verdict as unjust or shocking. Some Kosovo Albanians gathered outside the government building in Pristina reportedly threw stones, broke windows, toppled barricades and pushed police officers; anger was also reported in The Hague after the ruling was announced, with a brief scuffle involving Dutch police.

Albanian President Bajram Begaj and Prime Minister Edi Rama also criticised the verdict. Serbian Interior Minister Ivica Dacic welcomed the decision, while describing the Kosovo Liberation Army as a criminal organisation and a terrorist organisation. Serbian President Aleksandar Vucic also welcomed the convictions, but criticised the dropping of charges relating to crimes against humanity and said there should be no calls for celebration.

Presiding judge Charles Smith III stressed that the case concerned individuals, not the legitimacy of the Kosovo Liberation Army. The United Kingdom's Europe Minister Lord Wood said the findings concerned individuals and should not be used to fuel intercommunal or regional tensions. EU Commissioner for Enlargement Marta Kos said the decision concerned individual responsibility and justice for victims and families from all communities in Kosovo. Croatia's Foreign Ministry said the ruling did not change its position on the historical context of the Kosovo war and the repression of the Milosevic regime.
slots.packetTitle: Two sides of The Hague ruling

items.descriptionTR: Brentford manager Keith Andrews is full of praise after a resounding 3-0 win against West London rivals Chelsea, branding them "brilliant" following a unbeaten start to the Premier League campaign.
items.titleTR: 'We're unpredictable' - Andrews delighted with 'brilliant' Brentford

items.descriptionTR: Chelsea’s winless run in the Premier League stretched to three games as Brentford ran riot late on.
items.titleTR: How Brentford saw off Chelsea with three second-half goals in Premier League weekend opener

items.descriptionTR:
Chelsea manager Xabi Alonso criticised his players' game management after they were humbled 3-0 at Brentford, while defender Levi Colwill said his team were bullied at set pieces.
Brentford scored three second-half goals to ease past Chelsea, with Jaidon Anthony, Igor Thiago and Fabio Carvalho all scoring.
It was the third successive Premier League game in which Chelsea failed to win, having lost to Arsenal and drawn with Hull City last weekend.
While Chelsea have looked a threat in attack in their previous games, scoring 10 goals, defensively they look less than solid, with the three goals conceded at Brentford meaning they have been breached 12 times already.
Alonso is only the sixth manager to concede two or more goals in each of his first five Premier League matches in charge.
"I would say that we have dropped our consistency, our competitive mentality needed in the second half," Alonso said.
"I'm disappointed at the end with the second half and the result," Alonso said.
"This is not enough to compete in the Premier League, not to be able to go for the 90 minutes. This is why today we were punished. It's not about talking or looking for excuses."
"You know that the small details can be decisive. You don't have to give advantage in these kind of games. But it's about 95 minutes and we have not been able to keep that level throughout these few games in the start of the season and it's something that we'll have to do better."
Colwill said on Sky Sports that Chelsea were being "bullied" at set pieces. "It was tough. Maybe we overexposed ourselves [at 1-0 down] and they hit us on the counter-attack, which they're so good at," Colwill said.
"Second half we weren't good enough. We've got a lot to work on over the international break. Maybe at times we've been bullied [at set-pieces] and we have to improve at that. We can't rely on our front three to pull us of danger; we all need to help each other. We've got a lot of room to improve."
Alonso agreed with his captain, saying: "It's not just set pieces, but in duels, defence, in build-up, in and when we conceded first, but still we were in the game; but when you lose shape, you are out of control.
"So to be able to understand the game, to know what it takes to be competing until the end, is a process. It takes time for them to feel that. And at the moment we are not feeling it fully to compete for the whole game."
Keith Andrews LOVED @BrentfordFC's 3-0 win against Chelsea! ❤️ pic.twitter.com/TpGupnZKrF
— Premier League (@premierleague) September 18, 2026
Victory means Brentford remain unbeaten in the league heading into the international break, having won twice and drawn three.
"I was really looking forward to the game – the opposition have been setting up in a respectful way to nullify what we do," said Brentford boss Keith Andrews.
"I felt there was a performance bubbling, the approach was focused and in the second half we showed what we are. There's a really nice connection between the fans and players. We're enjoying the journey we're on. I love feeling that energy and how we play. We need to consistently evolve how we play."
The win moved Brentford up to third on nine points while Chelsea remain seventh on seven points.
items.titleTR: Bully boys: Brentford expose Chelsea's defensive woes

slots.packetSpot:
Brentford beat Chelsea 3-0 to extend their unbeaten Premier League run to five matches; with two wins and three draws, the team reached nine points and moved up to third place. After Jaidon Anthony scored from a corner, Igor Thiago made it 2-0 in the 83rd minute and Fabio Carvalho sealed the scoreline in stoppage time. It was Brentford's first home league win over Chelsea since 1938.

Chelsea remained seventh on seven points and failed to win for a third consecutive league match following their defeat to Arsenal and draw with Hull City. Xabi Alonso, the manager of the team that has conceded 12 goals in five league matches, said he was unhappy with the second-half performance and the refereeing, and that his side had been unable to compete for the full 90 minutes. Captain Levi Colwill said they had struggled physically at set pieces and had much to work on during the international break.

Keith Andrews praised Brentford's performance, hunger and humility.
slots.packetTitle: Brentford rise as Chelsea's questions deepen

items.descriptionTR: President Trump cut his weekend trip to Camp David short a day early, returning to Washington, D.C., on Saturday evening.  The president touched down at the Ellipse just before 8 p.m., according to a White House pool report. The White House’s official social media account shared a video clip of Trump departing Marine One.  The…
items.titleTR: Trump returns to White House as State Department issues security alerts for Middle East

items.descriptionTR:
￼
The US asked citizens in the region to watch for potential flight cancellations, airspace closures, and travel disruptions.
items.titleTR: US issues new warning to Americans in the Middle East

slots.packetSpot:
As warnings continue that clashes between Saudi Arabia and the Iran-backed Houthis could escalate, the US State Department called on its citizens in the Middle East to exercise greater caution. While urging preparedness for possible flight cancellations, airspace closures and travel disruptions, the department advised Americans outside the region to seriously reconsider travel to and through it.

Donald Trump’s decision to cut short his weekend schedule at Camp David and return to the White House on September 19 also coincided with the hours in which these developments unfolded. The White House did not explain the reason for the change in schedule.

An air raid alert and explosions were reported in Riyadh; Saudi authorities said a ballistic missile that the Houthis had launched at the capital was intercepted. The US warning also drew attention to the possibility that Iran and groups backed by Tehran could target US interests or locations linked to Americans.

items.descriptionTR:
President had brushed away suggestions to slow down AI technology, even as his own party counseled caution
Donald Trump on Saturday said he would appoint an artificial intelligence czar and create an “AI Force” to help monitor the technology, though he gave almost no details about either plan.
As global fears over AI have grown, especially in the past week in the face of multiple industry figures sounding the alarm about its dangers, the president has been critical of calls to slow down development of the fast-moving industry.
items.titleTR: Trump to create ‘AI Force’ to monitor technology as fears over out-of-control agents grow

slots.packetSpot:
Donald Trump announced that he plans to establish an “AI Force” to help monitor artificial intelligence in the United States and appoint an AI czar. In a social media post, he provided almost no details about the body's powers, members, legal basis or timetable.

The initiative emerged at a time of growing concern over the risks of artificial intelligence and calls for greater caution. Trump, however, opposes slowing AI development; he describes the concerns as a “hoax” and says his administration will not hinder the sector's growth. He also says malicious actors can be dealt with through criminal and civil justice systems.

Trump argued that the United States is ahead of China in artificial intelligence, while predicting that the technology could contribute up to 25 percent of the country's gross domestic product. California Governor Gavin Newsom, meanwhile, announced plans for a separate board that would develop safety regulations for AI companies in the state.

items.descriptionTR:
Warren Buffett has stepped down as chairman of Berkshire Hathaway and been named chairman emeritus with immediate effect, ending his more than six-decade tenure in the company’s top leadership role.
Mr Buffett, 96, is to remain on Berkshire’s board as a director and will continue to provide his “judgment and perspective”, the US company said on Friday.
His son, Howard, a Berkshire director since 1993, has been elected chairman of the board.
“Serving as your chairman has been the privilege of a lifetime, and I have never taken your trust for granted,” Mr Buffett said in a letter to shareholders. "Father Time always wins. He has, however, been generous with me. He has given me the opportunity to see Berkshire reach a point where I am more confident than ever about what lies ahead."
Greg Abel, who succeeded Mr Buffett as chief executive this year, will continue to run Berkshire’s operations, Berkshire said in a statement.
Mr Buffett joined Berkshire in 1965 and transformed the company from a struggling textile manufacturer into one of the world’s largest conglomerates, with businesses spanning insurance, energy, rail, manufacturing, services and retail.
In the letter to shareholders, Mr Buffett said the time was right to complete the leadership transition and praised Mr Abel for exceeding his expectations since taking over as chief executive.
“My son, Howard, will succeed me as chairman,” Mr Buffett said. “Greg runs the company; Howard will guard its culture and values – both worth more than anything on our balance sheet. Think of Howard as a policy the shareholders own and hope never to claim against.”
Howard Buffett has led the Howard G Buffett Foundation since 1999. Warren Buffett said he remained confident about Berkshire’s future and said the company was “in excellent hands”.
items.titleTR: Warren Buffett steps down as Berkshire Hathaway chairman after six decades

slots.packetSpot:
Warren Buffett’s departure from the chairmanship of Berkshire Hathaway is being presented as a new stage in a long-prepared management transition. While Buffett will remain on the board as honorary chairman, his son Howard Buffett will assume the chairmanship as part of the company’s succession plan.

The chief executive role had passed to Greg Abel after Buffett announced that he would step down from the position at the end of 2025. Howard Buffett’s main responsibility as chairman is said to be preserving Berkshire’s culture and values. By contrast, it is not yet known how active a role Warren Buffett will play in the company’s decisions under his new title.
slots.packetTitle: A changing of the guard at Berkshire

items.descriptionTR: Cuba was plunged into its seventh massive blackout of the year on Friday. The island of over nine million people endures constant power cuts due to the poor state of its aging thermoelectric plants – but the situation has worsened significantly since January, when Washington imposed a de facto energy blockade on the island. Story by Shirli Sitbon.
items.titleTR: Millions without power in Cuba as electrical grid collapses again

slots.packetSpot:
According to Cuba’s Energy Ministry, a grid-wide “total disconnection” on Friday left millions without electricity. UNE said a transmission failure, compounded by adverse weather conditions in central Cuba, triggered the outage; it announced that power had been restored by evening to some priority sites around hospitals and water pumping stations in Havana. Gradual repairs were continuing on Saturday.

This was at least the sixth partial or total outage of the year. As ageing infrastructure and chronic fuel shortages strain the electricity system, the Cuban government links the crisis to US sanctions and an oil blockade, while Washington blames poor domestic governance. Hospitals are struggling to maintain normal operations as shortages of food, medicine, water and cooking gas also persist; schools and public offices are being forced to close. The repeated outages are reportedly leading to rare protests.

items.descriptionTR:
Authorities accuse Ukraine of trying to disrupt poll and say 1,600 drones in total intercepted, while at least two people killed and oil refinery damaged
Hundreds of drones targeting Moscow and its surrounding region killed at least two people and damaged a major refinery on the final day of the country’s parliamentary elections, authorities said on Sunday.
The capital’s mayor said that more than 1,600 drones had been intercepted and shot down, 450 of which were aimed at Moscow.
items.titleTR: Hundreds of drones target Moscow on last day of voting in Russia’s parliamentary election

slots.packetSpot:
Russian authorities reported that a large-scale Ukrainian drone attack was launched against Moscow and its surrounding area on 20 September, the third and final day of the parliamentary election. Moscow Mayor Sergei Sobyanin described the attack as “unprecedented” and the “largest” against the capital; he said that more than 1,600 drones had been intercepted or shot down, with 450 reportedly headed for Moscow.

According to officials’ statements, two people were killed in the Moscow region; part of the Moscow oil refinery and a residential building were damaged. Russian officials alleged that the attack had been planned to disrupt the election and had not succeeded. Central Election Commission Chair Ella Pamfilova also said that more than 1,000 waves of DDoS attacks targeting election infrastructure had been recorded in recent days; no information was provided indicating that a link had been established between these digital attacks and the drone attack.
slots.packetTitle: Moscow skies at the ballot box

items.descriptionTR:
At least one person dead as stormy weather causes severe flooding in Barcelona and Valencia
Intense and slow-moving thunderstorms broke out on Wednesday afternoon across parts of eastern Spain, bringing some severe flooding and killing at least one person.
Storms first struck over the Castilla-La Mancha region during the afternoon before passing over Spain’s east coast, becoming very slow-moving and continuing overnight. Torrential rainfall, strong winds and large hail were reported in Valencia and Barcelona, causing widespread flooding in both cities. Weather stations west of Barcelona recorded some of the highest totals with more than 100mm (4in) of rain falling in the space of a few hours, and locally 70mm in just 30 minutes in the early hours of Thursday morning. Cars and roads were submerged, and flights were cancelled across the region.
items.titleTR: Weather tracker: Thunderstorms hit Spain as Japan braces for typhoon

items.descriptionTR: Intense rainfall dumped up to 96 mm on Torrent, south‑west of Valencia, flooding roads, homes and the Parc Central tunnel, trapping cars and prompting emergency pumping operations.
items.titleTR: Valencia region deluge leaves streets covered in mud and vehicles unusable in Torrent

slots.packetSpot:
Torrential rain and flash flooding affecting eastern and northeastern Spain on 17 September disrupted transport in Valencia and Catalonia; roads, railways and metro lines were affected, while flights were delayed and cancelled. According to authorities, the body of a man was recovered in Olivella after his vehicle was swept away by a current.

According to AVAMET data, more than 70 millimetres of rain fell in half an hour in some municipalities in Valencia province. Emergency services recorded 478 incidents in Valencia province, mostly involving property damage, water leaks and traffic disruption; in Catalonia, more than 850 calls were received and over 500 incidents were recorded. AEMET issued severe rainfall warnings, including a short-term red alert for the Barcelona coast.

Scientists say human-caused climate change is intensifying Mediterranean storms that strike eastern Spain in autumn. The rainfall came after Spain's hottest summer on record.

items.descriptionTR: Raids, arrests and internet restrictions imposed to ‘protect the family’ have persecuted LGBTQ+ groups while also hitting independent journalists and human rights organisations reporting on the police operation. Raids, arrests and internet restrictions imposed to ‘protect the family’ have persecuted LGBTQ+ groups while also hitting independent journalists and human rights organisations reporting on the police operation.
items.titleTR: Turkey Stages Wide-Ranging LGBT Crackdown for ‘Family Safety’

slots.packetSpot:
Coordinated police raids targeting LGBTİ+ organisations, clubs, cafés and homes in Turkey began on Saturday. By Thursday, courts in various provinces had sent at least 82 people to prison to stand trial in detention; Justice Minister Akın Gürlek said proceedings had been initiated against 162 people, nine associations and 13 businesses in 15 provinces. Those facing proceedings include LGBTİ+ activists and members of rights organisations, as well as people facing allegations of prostitution, drugs and other offences; not everyone arrested is accused of LGBTİ+ rights advocacy.

Gürlek said there would be no tolerance for criminal organisations, abuse networks and illegal activities targeting children, young people or families. Authorities reportedly used the obscenity law in the operations, and prosecutors were reportedly asked to increase investigations targeting the LGBTİ+ community. Istanbul-based SPoD and Ankara's KAOS GL are also named among the affected organisations.

Police who dispersed the protest outside Istanbul's main courthouse detained more than 100 people, including journalists; they were later released. Protests were also held outside Turkish embassies in Paris, Brussels, London, Oslo and Washington. The United Nations human rights office called for respect for human rights without discrimination on the basis of sexual orientation or gender identity, and for the immediate release of those held arbitrarily.

Human Rights Watch argues that the operations are intended to stigmatise LGBTİ+ people by portraying them as immoral and anti-family. As objections also rise from trade unions, medical organisations and opposition parties in Turkey, concerns are being voiced over further detentions, a shrinking space for living openly, and the risk of hate crimes.

items.descriptionTR: Coventry earned their first Premier League victory in 25 years after Jay Dasilva's winner and a controversial disallowed Nottingham Forest equaliser saw the promoted side win 1-0 at the City Ground.
items.titleTR: Coventry seal first PL win in 25 years at Forest amid VAR controversy

slots.packetSpot:
Coventry beat Nottingham Forest 1-0 at the City Ground in Nottingham on 19 September, thanks to Jay Dasilva's 55th-minute goal. According to the match account, the result was the team's first Premier League win in 25 years; it was also Coventry's first victory after starting the season with four matches without a point or a goal.

Nottingham Forest substitute Igor Jesus had an 86th-minute equaliser ruled out following a VAR review. Referee Jarred Gillett judged that Jesus had fouled Caleb Yirenkyi before the goal. Frank Lampard said the decision was correct, while Oliver Glasner said he did not want to talk about the matter and that what happened gave him a sense of deja vu.

Coventry also prevented an equaliser in the 76th minute when Bobby Thomas cleared the ball off the line. It was reported that Forest have yet to score or win at home in any competition this season; the team have won only once in the league at the City Ground since last December.
slots.packetTitle: Coventry's 25-year wait ends in VAR's shadow

items.descriptionTR:
Nine months after a quick injury sealed Joshua Van's win over Alexande Pantoja, Van won the rematch during UFC 331 at Crypto.com Arena Saturday.
￼
Joshua Van celebrates after defeating Alexandre Pantoja during a UFC 331 flyweight championship bout Saturday at Crypto.com Arena. (Luke Hales / Getty Images)
Alexandre Pantoja did not tap Joshua Van’s glove before the fight began. Nine months after an injury ended his reign as flyweight champion in just 26 seconds, the Brazilian returned to the Octagon to try to reclaim the belt that slipped away.
This time, no injury clouded the result. Pantoja came out determined to impose his style from the opening seconds, but Van found a way to keep him at a distance, counter with his boxing and survive the former champion’s take-down attempts.
After five rounds, the judges awarded the fight to the Van by unanimous decision, with scores of 49-46, 49-47 and 50-45.
Van retained the 125-pound title in the main event of UFC 331, held Saturday at Crypto.com Arena in front of a sold-out crowd of 19,357 fans. UFC CEO Dana White said the event generated $8.3 million in box office revenue, the highest in the arena’s history.
The result also vindicated Van’s claim to the championship.
In December 2025, Pantoja threw a high kick that Van caught. The Brazilian lost his balance and braced his left arm on the canvas to break his fall, but his elbow dislocated. The fight ended after 26 seconds and Van was awarded the belt.
￼
Joshua Van punches Alexandre Pantoja during their UFC 331 flyweight championship bout at Crypto.com Arena on Saturday. (Luke Hales / Getty Images)
Both fighters had much to gain during their return to the Octagon.
The animosity that had built up was evident from the start. As the fight began, Pantoja went straight for Van. The Brazilian scored an early takedown and sought to keep the champion on the mat, attempting to turn the fight into a grappling and ground-and-pound battle.
Van resisted and managed to get back to his feet. The lack of action during some early stretches prompted the first boos from the crowd.
But the pace changed.
Van began to find openings with his hands and Pantoja had to absorb strikes while continuing to seek takedowns. The champion also showed better defense against the Brazilian’s advances as the rounds progressed.
In the second round, the fight had to be briefly stopped after Pantoja claimed a headbutt. The strike was reviewed and determined to have been accidental, so the fight continued.
Read more:Alexandre Pantoja eager to reclaim belt he lost to Joshua Van in 26 seconds
“I don’t even know why he was getting worked up. He came at me throwing punches, and I was just trying to counter, and he simply hit me in the head,” Van said. “I guess … I have a tougher head. So then he started complaining and all that. He was saying, ‘You headbutted me, you’re cheating.’ And I told him, ‘You hit me!’ So… um … that was it.”
Van began to take greater control of the fight during the second and third rounds. His boxing allowed him to keep Pantoja at a distance and respond when the Brazilian tried to close in to take him down. Pantoja kept pressing, but he could no longer control the fight on the ground for extended periods.
The fourth round allowed the former champion to regain some of the control he’d lost. Pantoja managed to take Van down to the canvas again and worked from the top for much of the round, showing that he could still trouble the champion when he managed to impose his style.
Van, however, ended the fight on a high note.
“I knew I hurt him — you know, I knew I hurt him,” Van said. “He’s a mental giant, you know. He just didn’t want to go down. He doesn’t want to show that he’s hurt, but I know deep down he was hurt. But like I said, man, that’s why I respect him so much.”
In the fifth round, the champion landed a powerful right-hand punch that knocked Pantoja down. The Brazilian managed to recover and continue until the end, but the blow ultimately tipped the fight in Van’s favor.
￼
Alexandre Pantoja tries to pin Joshua Van on the ground during their UFC 331 flyweight championship bout at Crypto.com Arena on Saturday. (Luke Hales / Getty Images)
Ahead of the bout, Van defended his title in May against Tatsuro Taira, winning by technical knockout in the fifth round. Pantoja, on the other hand, hadn’t competed since his elbow injury against Van.
“There’s nothing to prove, man,” Van said. “Like I said, I knew I was going to win the first fight, too. So it’s like: ‘OK, do you guys want to see me win again?’”
Before the fight, tensions between the two had escalated. Van had insisted that his first victory wasn’t solely due to Pantoja’s injury, while the Brazilian argued that the December result didn’t show who was truly the better fighter.
The answer, this time, came after 25 minutes.
Tsarukyan knocks out Ruffy
￼
Arman Tsarukyan celebrates after earning a knockout win over Mauricio Ruffy during his UFC 331 lightweight bout at Crypto.com Arena on Saturday. (Luke Hales / Getty Images)
The co-main event of the night also ended sooner than expected.
Arman Tsarukyan and Mauricio Ruffy arrived at Crypto.com Arena with a five-round bout scheduled and key positions in the lightweight division on the line. Ruffy accepted the fight with just four weeks of preparation after Charles Oliveira was pulled from the card.
Ruffy came out ready to trade blows and showed speed in the opening minutes. Tsarukyan, as he had done for much of his career, sought to use his wrestling skills to change the pace of the fight.
Tsarukyan managed to drive Ruffy against the cage and began landing elbows. At the 4:56 mark of the first round, Tsarukyan landed two elbows that knocked Ruffy out and forced the referee to stop the fight.
“I came to Los Angeles to enjoy the city,” Tsarukyan said. “But I also came to win. I owe those elbows to one of my coaches who taught me how to use them.”
Get the best, most interesting and strangest stories of the day from the L.A. sports scene and beyond from our newsletter The Sports Report.
This story originally appeared in Los Angeles Times.
items.titleTR: Joshua Van beats Alexandre Pantoja again, defending his title at UFC 331 in L.A.

slots.packetSpot:
Joshua Van retained his title at 125 pounds by winning his UFC 331 rematch with Alexandre Pantoja by unanimous decision. The judges’ scores for the main event at Crypto.com Arena in Los Angeles were reported as 49-46, 49-47 and 50-45.

Their first meeting in December 2025 ended 26 seconds in after Pantoja dislocated his elbow, and the belt was awarded to Van. In the rematch, the result was decided after five rounds without the shadow of an injury.
slots.packetTitle: Van keeps the belt in Pantoja rematch

items.descriptionTR: England returned to the top of the T20 world rankings as they earned arguably their most emphatic win yet in a series of drubbings dished out to Sri Lanka, beating the tourists by eight wickets at Emirates Old Trafford.
items.titleTR: England swat aside Sri Lanka to return to top of T20 world rankings

slots.packetSpot:
England beat Sri Lanka by eight wickets in the third T20 match in Manchester, completing the series 3-0 and returning to number one in the T20 world rankings, according to Sky Sports. Sri Lanka were all out for 124 runs in 18.5 overs, while England reached the target of 125 runs in 9.4 overs.

Jos Buttler's unbeaten 62 runs off 32 balls and Harry Brook's 33 runs off 21 balls stood out in the victory. With this result, England's winning streak against Sri Lanka in T20 internationals reportedly reached 15. England were also reported to have won the previous two matches of the series by 119 runs and by six wickets.
slots.packetTitle: England back on top in T20s

items.descriptionTR: Warrington Wolves set up a Super League semi-final with Leeds Rhinos after a 35-12 victory over reigning champions Hull KR in their eliminator showdown at the Halliwell Jones Stadium.
items.titleTR: Warrington beat Hull KR to set up semi against Leeds as Hiku sees red

slots.packetSpot:
According to Sky Sports, Warrington Wolves reached the semi-finals by beating reigning champions Hull KR 35-12 in the Super League play-off match at Halliwell Jones Stadium. Matty Ashton scored a hat-trick for Warrington, who led 12-6 at half-time; Ben Currie, Albert Hopoate and Toby King were also among the scorers. Hull KR's tries came from Joe Burgess and Dean Hadley.

Peta Hiku was shown a red card for punching Warrington captain George Williams at the start of the second half. Sky Sports reports that Warrington took advantage of their numerical superiority. While the result ended Hull KR's title defence, it also reportedly brought Willie Peters' tenure as the club's head coach to an end.

Warrington will seek a place in the Grand Final in the semi-final scheduled to be played against Leeds Rhinos on 25 September.
slots.packetTitle: The champion's defence ends in Warrington

items.descriptionTR:
In his first major decision as Fed chair, Kevin Warsh raises interest rates by a quarter point and signals another increase before year-end
Kevin Warsh has been chair of the Federal Reserve for just four months, but this Wednesday will be remembered as the day he showed that he and his fellow governors, not outside forces, are the ones truly steering U.S. monetary policy. The Fed has done exactly what U.S. President Donald Trump did not want it to do under any circumstances: raise interest rates just six weeks before the midterm elections, in which Republicans risk losing control of Congress.
Seguir leyendo
items.titleTR: The Federal Reserve defies Trump with a unanimous rate hike six weeks before the midterms

items.descriptionTR:
￼
From mortgages to auto loans to credit cards, borrowing is set to get even pricier. But the Federal Reserve’s decision on September 16, 2026, to hike its baseline interest rate also highlighted an increasingly confounding dilemma: It can raise the price of money across the economy, but it can’t determine which sectors are most affected.
items.titleTR: Warsh’s rate hike a crapshoot for an already uneven US economy

items.descriptionTR: The Federal Reserve unanimously raised its benchmark rate by a quarter point as policymakers confront inflation that remains above target and uncertainty tied to geopolitical developments. Merrill and Bank of America Head of CIO Market Strategy Joe Quinlan tells Bloomberg This Weekend hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini that elevated diesel prices are a particular concern for businesses and could keep pressure on the Fed to raise rates further. (Source: Bloomberg)
items.titleTR: Diesel Prices Keep Pressure on Fed and Markets

items.descriptionTR:
The Federal Reserve just raised interest rates this week for the first time this year. So how does it actually work? And what does it mean for the economy — and the rest of us? Here are some answers. ￼
The Federal Reserve just raised interest rates this week for the first time this year. So how does it actually work? And what does it mean for the economy — and the rest of us? Here are some answers.
(Image credit: LM Otero)
￼
items.titleTR: Ever wonder how the Fed's interest rate actually works? We've got answers

slots.packetSpot:
The Federal Reserve unanimously raised its policy rate by 25 basis points on 16 September, bringing the target range to 3.75–4%. The decision was presented as the first increase in more than three years, with inflation, reported at an annual 3.4% in August, remaining above the bank's 2% target cited as the reason. The Fed also highlighted the relatively strong course of economic activity, employment, consumer spending, productivity and investment.

The move by the Fed, chaired by Kevin Warsh, came up against Donald Trump's public calls for interest rates to be cut. The view that the decision is a test of the central bank's capacity to act independently of political pressure has come to the fore. The possibility of another increase before the end of the year is also being signalled; however, it is noted that this is not a settled policy path.

Tighter monetary policy aims to cool demand and price pressures by making borrowing more expensive. It is assessed that this could have effects of varying weight on mortgages, credit cards, vehicle loans, small businesses and public borrowing; and that the housing market, which is particularly sensitive to high interest rates, could come under greater strain. By contrast, there is a view that artificial intelligence investments, fuelled by expectations of high returns, may be affected only to a limited extent. Oil and diesel prices linked to geopolitical developments are also cited among the factors keeping pressure on inflation and subsequent interest-rate decisions alive.
slots.packetTitle: The economy's uneven ground beneath the monetary brake

items.descriptionTR: President Trump said Friday that his son Donald Trump Jr. paid back the Russian oligarch who funded some of his lavish wedding celebrations after concerns flared over ethics violations and potential influences from foreign adversaries. President Trump was asked in the Oval Office whether it was appropriate that his son accepted the gift from Umar…
items.titleTR: Trump says son paid back Russian oligarch for wedding gift

items.descriptionTR:
The businessman, who accompanied Vladimir Putin on his recent trip to China, controls the country’s betting payment system and heads the opaque International Boxing Association, suspended by the IOC
The U.S. nonprofit journalism organization ProPublica has revealed that Umar Kremlev, a 43-year-old Russian businessman with close ties to the Kremlin, paid hundreds of thousands of dollars for Donald Trump Jr.’s wedding celebrations last May, and that another contractor for Russia’s Defense Ministry, Alexander Lagutin, was also invited to the event. Only one photo taken by a guest fleetingly shows Kremlev’s presence at the event, just days after both men accompanied Vladimir Putin on a trip to China.
Seguir leyendo
items.titleTR: Who is Umar Kremlev, the Russian magnate who paid for Donald Trump Jr.’s wedding festivities?

slots.packetSpot:
According to ProPublica, Russian businessman Umar Kremlev, who is said to have close ties to the Kremlin, paid hundreds of thousands of dollars toward some of the costs of Donald Trump Jr.’s wedding celebrations in the Bahamas. This included the rental of a private island, a fireworks display and other expenses.

Bettina Trump said Kremlev hosted the two-night celebrations and that it was a generous wedding gift; she stressed that the money did not finance only the private marriage ceremony attended solely by family members. Kremlev’s press office also said that he is friends with Trump Jr., that they met years ago and that he does not discuss politics with his American friends.

President Donald Trump said he understood that his son had reimbursed Kremlev for the expenses; that reimbursement has not been confirmed. Senator John Curtis described the arrangement as “corruption,” while Senator Thom Tillis called it “extremely bad.” Senate Majority Leader John Thune said he did not have enough information about the details.

Kremlev is known as the president of the International Boxing Association. Allegations concerning his ties to Vladimir Putin, Russian state-linked institutions and businesses in the betting sector are also in circulation. Alexander Lagutin, who is said to work for Russia’s Ministry of Defence, was reportedly invited to the celebration; Kremlev and Lagutin are also reported to have recently accompanied Putin on a trip to China.
slots.packetTitle: The shadow over a Bahamas celebration

items.descriptionTR:
Germany's Carsten Breuer and Canada's Jennie Carignan are battling it out to become to next chair of NATO's military committee.
BRUSSELS — NATO’s most senior commanders elect a new leader on Saturday in a consequential vote that will help shape how the alliance prepares for a potential Russian incursion and navigates persisting transatlantic tensions.
The alliance’s 32 chiefs of defense staff will elect a new chair of NATO’s most senior military body, the military committee, in Copenhagen in a hush-hush ballot — and choose between two candidates: Germany’s Gen. Carsten Breuer and Canada’s Gen. Jennie Carignan.
“NATO is in a very decisive moment and in a demanding spot — there’s a large conventional war raging in Europe and NATO is transforming itself again into a more robust, more European NATO,” said Janne Kuusela, Permanent Secretary at the Finnish defense ministry. “That of course means … we need the best possible individuals to fill these positions.”
Although little-known, NATO’s military committee is the alliance’s most senior military authority, with the chair expected to give honest military advice to allies — helping assess the feasibility, financing and capabilities of operations. They oversee dozens of working groups of NATO military staff, and broker consensus on formulating military advice.
The position is a “highly complex role,” said Eleonora Russell, the spokesperson of former chair Adm. Rob Bauer, because it requires simultaneously gaining the trust of both the military and the political leadership across the alliance — and not taking sides. 
Such a role is particularly challenging today given enduring transatlantic tensions, she said, and important as sensitive talks on NATO’s next four-year war planning cycle will kick off in October. “The trick is you have to be … an extremely good listener,” Russell said, “but then you have to also have a very strong backbone.”
Germany’s Breuer, who Berlin announced as a candidate in February, is seen as the front-runner, according to one NATO diplomat and two European national security officials, who were granted anonymity to speak freely about the sensitive matter.
Berlin is now Europe’s leading defense spender, the officials said, and the U.S. has previously nudged Germany toward leadership roles in the alliance as it seeks to reduce its military engagement on the continent. Strained bilateral ties between Ottawa and Washington might also make Carignan’s case more difficult, the officials said.
That support was on display in Washington on Jul. 23, when Breuer briefed Pentagon policy chief Elbridge Colby on Germany’s new military strategy. Colby later called the strategy “historic” and “highly laudable” and said Germany was positioning itself as “a key leader of Europe’s conventional defense” in a post on X.
“Both candidates are exceptional military leaders,” said another military official, who nonetheless wondered whether it was more important today to have a European in charge given the alliance’s push for the continent to take charge of its own defense, dubbed NATO 3.0.
Breuer’s pitch for the job has included its leadership role on NATO 3.0, the officials said, as well as the four-star general’s strong existing relationships with his counterparts since he took over as Germany’s chief of defense in 2023.
Carignan, Ottawa’s top general since 2024, has focused her campaign on reinvigorating the role of the military committee, the officials said, and signaling enduring transatlantic unity inside NATO. That comes as the alliance has repeatedly been rocked by feuds with U.S. President Donald Trump since he retook office last year.
Germany’s defense ministry didn’t respond to a request for comment. A spokesperson for Canada’s defense ministry said Carignan’s “candidacy reflects Canada’s enduring commitment to NATO and to strengthening collective defence and transatlantic security.”
Out of sight, out of mind
Yet the campaign is enigmatic and behind closed doors — all the way down to the blind vote.
That’s because “the whole point of this is for this to be a military group of professionals who trust each other,” Russell said, since “on the military level you need to have boundless loyalty, and if you know exactly who voted for you and who didn’t, then you lose that.”
To ensure that loyalty, the vote count will stop once a majority — or 17 votes — is reached, leaving the real result unknown, one NATO official said. Adding to the mystery, some chiefs of defense are under strict instructions by their ministries to vote for one candidate, the official said, while others can make up their own minds. 
Behind the scenes, the candidates have lobbied their counterparts through letters, face-to-face pitches with NATO ambassadors, at security summits and with phone calls to ministries, said the three officials. 
Since Berlin nominated Breuer, he has been a frequent visitor to NATO capitals. His recent stops have included Albania, North Macedonia, the U.S., Slovenia, Latvia and Estonia — all in the past two months. Breuer has used trips and meetings with fellow military leaders to make the case for Germany’s candidacy, said a person familiar with the effort.
The next military committee chair is expected to take over from Italy’s Adm. Giuseppe Cavo Dragone next July, the same NATO official said.
items.titleTR: Inside the secret race to become NATO’s next top general

items.descriptionTR: BRUSSELS, Sept 19 - General Carsten Breuer, Germany's chief of defence, was chosen on Saturday as the next head of NATO's military committee, the alliance's top military authority and a key advisory body for its political leaders.
items.titleTR: German general Breuer elected to head top NATO military body

slots.packetSpot:
The result of the secret ballot for the chairmanship of NATO’s Military Committee, contested by Canada’s Jennie Carignan and Germany’s Carsten Breuer, has been announced. According to Reuters, the defence chiefs of the 32 member countries elected Breuer as the committee’s next chair.

Breuer will replace Italian Admiral Giuseppe Cavo Dragone next summer. The chair of the committee, NATO’s highest military authority, serves as a bridge between the alliance’s political leadership and military commanders and acts as Secretary General Mark Rutte’s principal military adviser.

Before the vote, the Canadian government had supported Carignan’s candidacy, and it had been stated that, if elected, Carignan would become the first woman to chair the committee in the alliance’s 77-year history. It was unclear what the US approach to this candidacy would be.

items.descriptionTR:
The enigmatic tiger cats of South America now encompass a new species – the tilcayo – bringing the number of known tiger cat species to five
￼

The tilcayo (Leopardus tilcayo) in an animal refuge in La Paz, Bolivia
Paola Nogales-Ascarrunz
A new cat species has been scientifically described – the diminutive, spotted tilcayo from Bolivia.
Several species of small cat in the Leopardus genus live in South America, including the ocelot, margay, kodkod, Geoffroy’s cat and the tiger cat or oncilla. The similar appearance of these nocturnal and hard-to-spot cats has made separating them into distinct species difficult.
This is particularly true of tiger cats, which are about the size of a house cat, and are found in Costa Rica in Central America, and across a vast swathe of South America including Bolivia, Brazil, Venezuela, Colombia, Ecuador and Peru. Historically, there have been many local and scientific names for them, but they all got subsumed into a single species, Leopardus tigrinus.
Advertisement

Read more
Tiny orange frog around the size of a pencil tip is brand-new species
Genetic studies have since divided the species into four, resurrecting three of the species names that scientists once used before they were all lumped together under the name L. tigrinus. This process saw the official recognition of the southern tiger cat (Leopardus guttulus) in 2013, Leopardus emiliae in 2017 and the clouded tiger cat (Leopardus pardinoides) in 2024.
Now, Eduardo Eizirik at the Pontifical Catholic University of Rio Grande do Sul (PUCRS) in Porto Alegre, Brazil, and his colleagues have analysed the complete genomes of 38 individuals from the Leopardus genus, including 26 tiger cats from across their known range.
The genomics revealed a fifth distinct species living in the Bolivian Yungas forests on the east slopes of the Andes mountains. The researchers describe it under a completely new name: Leopardus tilcayo, naming it after the local term used for this cat.
Subscriber-only newsletter
Sign up to Editor’s Highlights

Sign up to newsletter
￼
“We’ve discovered a new species of cat that had not been scientifically named before,” says Eizirik, adding that this is the first time this has happened for a century.
“There are more cat species. Who can’t love that?” says Leslie Lyons at the University of California, Davis. “They’re hard to find and see, so it’s not surprising that some of the early taxonomy needs to be modified now we have more data.”
L. tilcayo has a combined head and body length of between about 42 and 50 centimetres and weighs between 1.5 and 2 kilograms. The genomes revealed that it diverged from the lineage containing L. tigrinus and L. pardinoides nearly 1.4 million years ago.
￼
Origin story of domestic cats rewritten by genetic analysis
Domestic cats originated in North Africa and spread to Europe in the past 2000 years, according to DNA evidence, while in China a different species of cat lived alongside people much earlier
Telling the new species apart visually is not easy. “The five tiger cat species are all cryptic species. They’re morphologically very similar,” says team member Jonas Lescroart at University of Antwerp in Belgium.
The researchers also found that in the Peruvian Yungas forests, on the west side of the Andes, there is a distinct group of cats in the L. tigrinus lineage that they describe as a novel subspecies, L. tigrinus antisuyo.
There are so many barriers in South America that can geographically isolate animal populations from each other, including mountains and rivers, that more cat species may be waiting to be found, says Lyons. “It’d be rather cool if we could find another species out there.”
L. tigrinus is listed as vulnerable by the IUCN Red List, but the new species and subspecies will have to be evaluated and protected as distinct units, says Eizirik, especially as the forests they live in are shrinking as agriculture expands.
Journal Reference:
Current Biology DOI: 10.1016/j.cub.2026.08.059
items.titleTR: Beautiful new cat species is first to be named in a century

slots.packetSpot:
The tilcayo, which lives in Bolivia’s Yungas cloud forests, was identified as a distinct wildcat species under the scientific name Leopardus tilcayo in a study published by researchers in Current Biology. According to the study, it is the first living cat species to be formally named and described in more than a century.

The cat, which local communities call tilcayo, is reported to have a light brown coat with irregular rosettes and to reach about 46 centimetres in length and three pounds in weight. Examining the DNA of 38 cats from various South American countries — including eight museum specimens — the team concluded that tiger cats comprise five genetically distinct species. The tilcayo lineage is estimated to have diverged from the others about 1.4 million years ago.

Knowledge of the species’ biology is for now limited to two live individuals and a small number of camera-trap records. Faecal samples indicate that small rodents may be among its foods, while camera traps suggest it may be more active at night. As deforestation, agricultural expansion, human-caused fires and mining pressure continue in the Yungas, the findings were submitted to the IUCN; the five lineages are expected to be considered separately in the upcoming assessment.

items.descriptionTR: Authorities in north-central Nigeria are investigating the deaths of 37 people while they were in custody for illegal mining. Officials say the detainees died at a detention facility in Niger state, with the Nigerian Security and Civil Defence Corps pointing to a possible disease outbreak. However, some reports suggest overcrowding and poor ventilation may have contributed to the deaths. Details by FRANCE 24 correspondent Sam Olukoya.
items.titleTR: 37 die in Nigerian custody: Reports blame overcrowding, government disputes claim

items.descriptionTR:
Police fire teargas as protests break out in city of Minna after deaths of suspected illegal goldminers, many of whom were children
Survivors from a prison cell in Nigeria where 37 suspected illegal goldminers died while in the custody of a paramilitary group this week have recounted their panic and struggle for breath, as police on Friday fired teargas at people protesting against the deaths and imposed an overnight curfew in the city of Minna.
The victims – many of whom were children – were found dead on Thursday in the cells of the Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps (NSCDC), which had raided suspected illegal goldmines and ⁠locked up dozens of miners in the city, the state capital of the mineral-rich state of Niger.
items.titleTR: Survivors recount panic and struggle to breathe in Nigerian prison cell where 37 died

items.descriptionTR: [Premium Times] The Niger State Government has imposed a 24-hour curfew across Minna, the state capital, as tension rises over the deaths of about 37 suspected illegal miners in the custody of the Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps (NSCDC).
items.titleTR: Nigeria: Niger State Imposes 24-Hour Curfew After Suspects Die in Custody

slots.packetSpot:
In Nigeria's Niger State, the cause of the deaths of 37 people detained on suspicion of illegal mining while in NSCDC custody remains unclear. The NSCDC initially referred to a possible disease outbreak; an intelligence note shared with AFP pointed instead to overcrowding and inadequate ventilation. Accounts by survivors and relatives point to conditions in the cell, while at least one of those accounts has not been independently verified.

In Minna, police used tear gas following protests and reported attacks on public buildings; a Reuters reporter said security forces fired live ammunition. The state government imposed a 24-hour curfew, halted mining, cancelled an APC rally and declared three days of mourning. NSCDC state commander Suberu Siyaka Aniviye and his team were suspended pending the investigation; Governor Mohammed Bago stressed that this was not a declaration of guilt. Reviews launched by the police and state authorities are continuing.

items.descriptionTR:
Authorities ban anti-immigration march after fireworks and other projectiles thrown at officers in city centre park
Dutch riot police dispersed several hundred far-right protesters in The Hague on Saturday after violence erupted and local authorities banned a planned march in the city against immigration and asylum policies.
The Dutch public broadcaster NOS reported that 24 people had been arrested, after some protesters threw fireworks and other projectiles at police.
items.titleTR: Dutch riot police break up violent far-right protest in The Hague

slots.packetSpot:
Violence broke out at a far-right protest against immigration and asylum policies held at the Malieveld in central The Hague. The municipality banned the planned march; the crowd was then ordered to disperse, and Dutch riot police dispersed several hundred protesters.

According to The Guardian, some protesters threw fireworks and other objects at police. According to NOS, 24 people were detained; police were also reported to have used pepper spray and water cannon. The detentions were said to be linked to various allegations, including failure to comply with the dispersal order and illegal possession of weapons.

Justice Minister David van Weel said of the protest organised by the far-right We Are the People group that demonstrators gave Nazi salutes, chanted antisemitic slogans and attacked police. Prime Minister Rob Jetten said the protesters deliberately sought confrontation with police and chanted far-right and antisemitic slogans.
slots.packetTitle: Far-right protest broken up in The Hague

items.descriptionTR:
Three pupils were killed in a school shooting on the southern Philippines island of Mindanao on ⁠Friday, including the 16-year-old suspected gunman who turned the weapon on himself.
Eight people were injured, with four in critical condition. The victims were ⁠all pupils at the school, aged 14 to 17, said Albert Palencia, mayor of Banga town in ⁠South Cotabato, where the shooting took ‌place.
“The suspect supposedly sat beside his friends and told them to go home 'because after lunch, I will be executing my plan',” Mr Palencia told Reuters. “His friends laughed because the shooter was a known joker. After lunch, he started shooting students. He hit 10 students before killing himself.”
South Cotabato governor Reynaldo Tamayo urged ⁠parents to ensure guns are kept out of reach of their children.
“We need to be responsible in storing firearms,” he said. “Gun owners, in particular, must make sure that minors do not have access to them.
“We cannot expect a handful of security personnel to monitor thousands of students. We need to work together because otherwise this will be very difficult for us to address.”
Last month, a pupil live-streamed himself shooting and killing another pupil in a classroom in Zamboanga City in the southern Philippines before taking his own life.
In June, at least three pupils were killed and 20 injured in an attack at a public high school in Tacloban in the eastern Philippines, where two classmates opened fire on campus.
The Philippines has relatively strict ‌gun ownership regulations, including background ⁠checks and psychological evaluation requirements, although illegal firearms remain in circulation.
items.titleTR: Three dead including teenage gunman in Philippines school shooting

slots.packetSpot:
A shooting was reported at a school in Banga, South Cotabato, in the southern Philippines. According to authorities, three students were killed, including the 16-year-old suspected attacker, who was said to have turned the gun on himself. Eight students were injured; four were reported to be in critical condition.

Banga Mayor Albert Palencia said the suspect appeared to have fired indiscriminately at students in a nearby classroom after leaving his Grade 9 classroom. According to Palencia’s account, the suspect brought to school a 9mm pistol belonging to his father, who works at the Department of Education, after gaining access to the safe where it was kept. South Cotabato Governor Reynaldo Tamayo called on gun owners to store firearms in a way that keeps them out of children’s reach.

Fatal school shootings had also been reported in Zamboanga and Tacloban since June. Despite relatively strict rules on acquiring firearms in the Philippines, illegal weapons are said to be in circulation.

items.descriptionTR:
France is loaning the New Spain-era manuscript that chronicles the founding, splendor, and fall of Tenochtitlan to the National Museum of Anthropology and History
The Azcatitlan Codex, a 50‑folio summary of the Aztec empire’s history, has temporarily returned to Mexico on loan from France to mark the 200th anniversary of diplomatic relations between the two countries. The document left Mexico in 1840 and has come back nearly two centuries later to be exhibited for three months at the National Museum of Anthropology and History in Mexico City. Mexican president Claudia Sheinbaum and French president Emmanuel Macron agreed in November 2025 to exchange this codex and the Boturini Codex to mark the relaunch of Franco‑Mexican relations.
Seguir leyendo
￼
items.titleTR: The Azcatitlan Codex returns to Mexico from Europe after nearly two centuries

slots.packetSpot:
The Azcatitlan Codex has been brought to Mexico on loan from France for the first time since 1840. The manuscript, which will be displayed for three months at the National Museum of Anthropology and History in Mexico City, is part of a reciprocal exchange of codices organised to mark the 200th anniversary of diplomatic relations between France and Mexico.

According to reports, Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum and French President Emmanuel Macron agreed in November 2025 on the exchange of the Azcatitlan and Boturini codices. While the Azcatitlan is in Mexico, the Boturini Codex, prepared in the 16th century and recounting the journey from Aztlán to Tenochtitlan, will go on display at the Bibliothèque Nationale de France in Paris from next week. Both works are expected to be returned to their host countries in December.

Dating to the late 17th century, the 50-leaf Azcatitlan Codex recounts the history of the Aztec empire: the migration from Aztlán, the founding of Tenochtitlan, the reigns of rulers, the arrival of the Spanish in 1519 and the caste system in New Spain. It is stated that the Mexican government has no intention of seeking the return of the work, which is held in the collection of the Bibliothèque Nationale de France under the supervision of the French government.
slots.packetTitle: A reciprocal journey of two codices

items.descriptionTR:
￼
The lone juror who wanted to convict Lindsay Clancy of murder for killing her three children said he was certain of her guilt, but that other jurors wouldn’t listen to him, according to a statement released by his lawyer Friday in his first public comments on the case.
items.titleTR: Lindsay Clancy holdout juror breaks silence, says he didn't have 'any doubts' of her guilt

slots.packetSpot:
Michael Desronvil, the lone holdout juror in the Lindsay Clancy case, said in a public statement that he had no doubt Clancy was guilty. Desronvil said he believed the physical evidence, key witnesses and the case presented by the prosecution showed that Clancy had planned to kill her children.

Clancy had admitted killing her three children; her lawyers had argued that she was experiencing postpartum psychosis. The prosecution contended that the killings were premeditated. On September 4, the judge declared a mistrial because the jury could not reach a unanimous verdict after about 40 hours of deliberation; no conviction was entered against Clancy.

While the jury was reported to have split 11 to 1 in favor of finding that Clancy bore no criminal responsibility, accounts of the deliberations differ. Some jurors criticized Desronvil, while Clancy’s lawyer Kevin Reddington argued that he had not applied the principle of reasonable doubt. It was not disclosed whether the prosecution would seek a retrial; the next hearing will be held on September 29 at Plymouth Superior Court.

items.descriptionTR: An Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) officer pleaded not guilty Friday to federal charges stemming from allegations that he lied to authorities about what led up to the January shooting of a Venezuelan man during Minneapolis enforcement operations. A federal grand jury indicted Christian Castro, 52, in early September on six counts of making materially…
items.titleTR: ICE officer pleads not guilty to lying to FBI about Minneapolis shooting

slots.packetSpot:
ICE officer Christian Castro’s not-guilty pleas to federal and state charges related to the shooting of Julio Cesar Sosa-Celis in Minneapolis have brought the dispute over the account of the incident into court proceedings.

The federal case consists of six charges alleging that Castro made false statements to the FBI. In the separate case in Hennepin County, there are four counts of second-degree assault and one count of making a false crime report. Castro reportedly said that he was attacked with a broom handle and a snow shovel before firing; prosecutors and Hennepin County Attorney Mary Moriarty reportedly argued that this account was fabricated.

Venezuela-born Sosa-Celis was reportedly treated for a bullet wound to his thigh. Castro was placed on administrative leave and suspended without pay while the cases proceed; following his detention in Texas, he returned to Minnesota to face the charges.
slots.packetTitle: Two cases from a shooting in Minneapolis

items.descriptionTR:
At least 16 people were killed ⁠in north-western Pakistan on Friday ⁠when a suicide attacker rammed an explosives-laden car into a police complex ⁠as people were praying at a mosque inside.
Five police ⁠officers were among ‌the dead after the vehicle smashed into the outer wall and gunmen who accompanied it opened fire in the city of Kohat, provincial police chief Zulfikar Hameed said.
The Interior Ministry said in a post on X that there had been a blast near a police site in the Kohat district of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province. Officials said 57 people were injured.
The ministry expressed ⁠its grief over the loss of ‌life and said the "cowardly actions" of the attackers could ‌not weaken the "nation's firm resolve". Mr Hameed described the incident as a suicide attack.
All seven attackers were killed in the ‌explosion and the gun battle ⁠that followed, police said in a statement. Videos shared by rescuers showed the boundary wall ripped apart by the blast, and people trying to pull the wounded from the debris as ambulances arrived.
The blast occurred close to a mosque where the police personnel, their family members and other civilians were offering Friday prayers, police said.
Local media has reported that an operation is under way to look for survivors, while the death toll may rise.
￼
There was no immediate claim of responsibility. Tehrik-e-Taliban, the Pakistani branch of the Taliban and the region's main militant group, issued a statement disowning Friday's attack.
In recent months, militancy in Pakistan's border areas has surged, with the military and police the main targets. Islamabad says militants use safe havens in Afghanistan to train and plan attacks in Pakistan. Afghanistan's Taliban government has denied the allegation and said the militancy is a problem for Pakistan.
items.titleTR: At least 16 killed in Pakistan car bomb attack near mosque

slots.packetSpot: A car bomb reportedly exploded near a mosque and a police compound in Kohat, northwestern Pakistan, on Friday. Police and rescue officials spoke of at least 21 dead and 80 injured, while the figure in the headline was given as at least 16 dead. Police said armed men tried to enter the compound and that a gunfight broke out; no one claimed responsibility for the attack.
slots.packetTitle: Blast by a mosque in Kohat, death toll unclear

items.descriptionTR:
Four of Nurat Osman’s alleged abductors were killed during rescue after she was taken from outside her home last week
A British woman kidnapped in Malawi last week has been rescued by police after a shootout in which four of her alleged abductors were killed.
Nusrat Osman was abducted outside her home in the southern city of Blantyre on 11 September at about 12.30pm. Police had offered a reward of 30m Malawi kwacha (£12,950) for information leading to her rescue and the arrest of the perpetrators.
items.titleTR: British woman who was kidnapped in Malawi rescued by police after shootout

slots.packetSpot:
According to Malawi police, 47-year-old British national Nusrat Osman, who was born in Leicester, was rescued on Thursday in an operation outside Blantyre after being abducted by four unidentified people in the city's Mount Pleasant neighbourhood on 11 September. It was announced that an armed clash occurred during the operation; the four suspected abductors, said to have been carrying AK-47 rifles and pistols, died in the hospital to which they were taken with injuries.

Deputy Inspector General of Police Noel Kayira, who took part in the operation, was reported to have been wounded by gunfire and to be in a stable condition in hospital. Osman, who was reunited with her family, was said to have been taken to hospital for treatment and physical and psychological assessment, and to still be experiencing trauma.

The motive for the abduction is unknown; the identities of the dead suspects and how the group was found were not disclosed. Police announced that there had been no known ransom demand or communication from the abductors after the incident, and that the investigation was continuing. A reward of 30 million Malawian kwacha had been offered for information leading to Osman's rescue and to those responsible being caught and convicted; the UK Foreign Office had also previously said it was in contact with Malawian authorities.
